newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM DAMPENS EARLY POLL SPECULATION AFTER WIN.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM DAMPENS EARLY POLL SPECULATION AFTER WIN.

text.p: Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, after his coalition's win in Senate elections on Saturday, further dampened specualtion that his minority government might use the victory to seek early general elections.

While leaving his party's headquarters on Saturday, Klaus was asked if the results confirmed his opinion, given after last week's first-round Senate vote, that early elections to the lower house should not be necessary.
"I think they did," he told Reuters. He did not elaborate.
His three-party conservative coalition won 52 seats after this weekend's runoffs for the 81-seat Senate.

Saturday's result, after the opposition Social Democrats stripped the government of its lower house majority in June general elections, appeared to show public opinion moving back toward the centre-right coalition.

Analysts viewed the elections to the Senate, which has limited legislative power, more as a guage for whether the coalition or the opposition would be in a position to seek a majority in the lower house through an early poll.

After last week's first-round Senate vote, which gave Klaus's Civic Democratic Party the potential to win up to 79 seats, Klaus told Czech Television: "This country does not need another (lower house) election. It needs to function, work."
The opposition Social Democrats won 25 Senate seats, while the junior coalition parties, the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) and Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) won 13 and seven seats respectively.
But voter turnout of only 30 percent made it hard for anybody to draw conclusions on what might be the result if early elections to the more powerful lower house were called.
